production.title: Claude Artifacts Just Got a Huge Upgrade

narration:
Claude just dropped a feature that allows you to install an artifact
as a real app right on your Mac or Windows computer.
So that little tracker or dashboard that you or your team use,
Claude can now build that right on your desktop.
So in this video, I’m going to show you how these new apps work,
the other big upgrades that make artifacts one of the most
important Claude features to be getting good at right now,
and the real risk of getting locked into Claude’s ecosystem.
So let’s get right into it.
An installed artifact gets its own desktop icon
and window instead of opening inside Claude.
The way this works is you actually build an artifact just like normal.
And then when you open it up inside of the Claude desktop app,
you just go to share or you click on the name of the artifact,
and then you can hit install as app,
and then it gets its own icon and it opens up in its
own window like any other app on your actual laptop or desktop.
This app can still use Claude and all of your connectors.
It can send you notifications or sit in
your menu bar or your system tray,
and it updates itself whenever you actually update the artifact.
There’s no API key or anything else to set up.
Now, right now it is in beta, and it literally just dropped.
And anything made from a template like your docs, slides,
or sheets can’t be installed.
And if an app asks you for access to your computer,
like running programs or changing local files,
only allow it for apps you built or
really trust because Anthropic doesn’t automatically review these.
But anyways, apps are just the newest upgrade to artifacts.
Over the last few months,
Anthropic has turned artifacts into something that your
whole team can really work out of.
And people have made more than 45 million
docs or decks and designs with artifacts.
Anthropic defines an artifact as anything that Claude makes
for you that you’d put in front of someone, like a design, a deck,
a doc, a dashboard, or maybe a small interactive tool.
Basically, it’s a page that Claude builds that lives at a live public link.
And right now, there are 7 templates.
We’ve got docs, slides, design, data, sheets, whiteboards, and motion for short animated explainers.
And then every update that you make is
just a new version of that same link.
The hard part here was never getting Claude to be able to make something.
But now with Artifacts, you can just have Claude build it,
and then you can hit share,
and then your team just opens up a link, and it’s super simple.
I don’t think that artifacts will replace Excel or your CRM,
at least not yet.
Anthropic even says Sheets only has simple spreadsheet functionality for now.
And if you need a real app with real
login and real backend and real role-based access control,
then you’ll probably want to go with something that you actually
deploy yourself or some other solution that’s built for that.
What I think Artifacts replaces is like the small software, right?
Like every team has little things they either
pay a subscription for or never build,
like a hiring tracker or an onboarding checklist or
a training quiz or a weekly KPI page,
or I think you guys get the picture, right?
And now each one is basically just a prompt and a link.
And then just tell Claude,
“Turn this into a shared artifact that my team can open from a link.
Make it easy to update every week and show where every number came from.”
And now the last thing I wanted to address,
because some of you might be thinking,
if everything about your business lives inside of Claude, like as an artifact,
aren’t you just locking yourself into Claude Code or into Anthropic?
And it’s a very fair concern.
Artifact content, yes, it is stored on Anthropic’s infrastructure.
People in your organization have to sign into Claude to see it.
Every big AI company is kind of doing some version
of this because they’re realizing the model alone might not
be the moat heading into the next couple of years.
So they’re all building the place where your work actually lives.
But of course,
all of these artifacts have their own sort of like exit door.
You can export them to Word or PDF or Google Docs or PowerPoint slides,
Sheets, CSV, HTML, whatever you want.
The rule for these artifacts is pretty simple,
which is basically just keep the source of truth in places
you own and then just use artifacts as the window.
It’s less about Claude-specific artifacts.
It’s really more about knowing how to brief
AI to build what your team needs, how to check it,
how to share it,
how to get people working from a link instead of a file.
And I think that all of these skills will
carry over to whatever tool ends up winning.
Bet on the habit and the skill of
working that way rather than one specific tool.
Follow us for more.

research.summary: Anthropic launched “Install as app” for eligible Claude Artifacts on November 24, 2026. The beta lets users turn custom Artifacts into Mac or Windows desktop apps with their own window and icon, while retaining access to Claude and connected apps. The feature requires Claude Desktop, an internet connection, and a signed-in Claude account; it is not a fully independent offline app. Anthropic warns that installed Artifacts can request operating-system permissions, including file access and program execution, and says it does not review apps before installation. The video’s broader claims about Artifacts as team tools, seven templates, private-by-default sharing, storage, and the 45-million creation figure are supported by Anthropic’s current documentation. The “ecosystem lock-in” point is an analytical concern rather than a directly measurable Anthropic claim.

claims.claim: Anthropic announced Install as app on November 24, 2026, allowing eligible Claude Artifacts to become Mac and Windows desktop apps in beta.
claims.source_title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps

claims.claim: An installed Artifact receives its own icon and window, can be shared, can use Claude and connected apps, and updates when the underlying Artifact is edited.
claims.source_title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps

claims.claim: Installing an Artifact requires Claude for Mac or Claude for Windows version 6.28899.0 or later; the feature is rolling out in beta across Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise plans.
claims.source_title: Install an artifact as an app

claims.claim: Users install an Artifact by opening it in Claude Desktop, choosing the Artifact title menu, right-click menu, or Share menu, selecting Install as app, and confirming the installation.
claims.source_title: Install an artifact as an app

claims.claim: Installed Artifact apps must be online and signed in to Claude Desktop when opened; they are not standalone offline applications.
claims.source_title: Install an artifact as an app

claims.claim: Installed Artifacts can request permissions for notifications, keyboard shortcuts, floating above other windows, menu-bar or system-tray items, and full computer access. Full access can allow an app to run programs and read, change, or delete files without asking each time.
claims.source_title: Install an artifact as an app

claims.claim: Anthropic says it does not review installed Artifact apps before installation; users should give full computer access only to apps they made or fully trust.
claims.source_title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps

claims.claim: Building an app and requests it makes to Claude count toward the user’s normal plan usage limits, and no separate API key or login is required because the app uses the user’s Claude account.
claims.source_title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps

claims.claim: At launch, Artifacts made from templates such as Claude Docs, Slides, and Sheets cannot be installed as apps; legacy Artifacts and live Artifacts from Claude Cowork also cannot be installed.
claims.source_title: Install an artifact as an app

claims.claim: Anthropic defines an Artifact as something Claude makes that a user might put in front of someone, including a design, deck, document, dashboard, or small interactive tool.
claims.source_title: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

claims.claim: Claude’s current Artifact templates are Docs, Slides, Design, Data, Sheets, Whiteboards, and Motion. Data is available on paid plans; Sheets and Whiteboards are beta on paid plans; Motion is beta on Team and Enterprise plans.
claims.source_title: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

claims.claim: Artifacts start private by default. Depending on the plan, users can share with invited people, their organization, or anyone with the link; Team and Enterprise administrators can control external sharing.
claims.source_title: Share artifacts

claims.claim: Artifacts can connect to apps such as Asana, Google Calendar, and Slack through connected apps or custom connectors, and they can store personal or shared data between sessions.
claims.source_title: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

claims.claim: Anthropic documents a default Artifact storage limit of up to 100 MB or 25,000 saved records, whichever is reached first; uploaded files can be up to 20 MB each, with a 5,000-file and 1 GB total limit.
claims.source_title: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

claims.claim: Claude Code can publish session output as a live interactive Artifact at a private URL, and the page updates as the session continues.
claims.source_title: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

claims.claim: As of October 8, 2026, Anthropic said users had created more than 45 million Docs, decks, and designs in Claude. This figure covers those three categories, not all Artifact types.
claims.source_title: Build live dashboards and animate explainers with Claude

claims.claim: Anthropic’s October 8, 2026 update said teams can work on the same doc, deck, design, or dashboard; share selected outputs outside the organization when permitted; and export decks to PowerPoint, PDF, or editable Google Slides.
claims.source_title: Build live dashboards and animate explainers with Claude

core_fact.fact: On November 24, 2026, Anthropic introduced a beta feature that lets users install eligible Claude Artifacts as apps on Mac and Windows, giving them their own desktop window and icon while allowing access to Claude, connectors, and selected operating-system capabilities.

metadata.title: Claude Artifacts Just Became Real Desktop Apps
metadata.description:
See how Claude Artifacts become real Mac and Windows desktop apps, plus the biggest Claude upgrades and the risks of relying on Claude for your team.

Free guide to this video (steps and every source): https://studio.golidee.com/guides/golide-long-2026-11-27.pdf

You’ll learn how to install an Artifact as an app, use notifications and connectors, and build simple tools like trackers, dashboards, checklists, quizzes, and KPI pages without traditional software development.

We’ll also look at what Claude Artifacts can replace, what they still cannot do, how to export your work, and how to avoid getting locked into one AI platform.

Chapters
0:00 Intro
0:27 Installed Apps
1:28 Artifact Basics
2:24 Small Team Tools
3:15 Lock-In Risk
4:01 Close

#Claude #ClaudeAI #ClaudeArtifacts #AIApps #AIAutomation #AIPproductivity #Anthropic

Music: Pulsar by The Grey Room / Density & Time
